subject: neighbour impute uses random method for some samples

messages.author: 1eb81fa619cb344d
messages.subject: neighbour impute uses random method for some samples
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have a question about using the gl.impute function using "neighbour" as the impute method. I used the following filtering steps / thresholds after inspection of the dartR report functions for my dataset:
  1. Secondaries were removed from the SNP dataset
  2. Dataset was filtered on reproducibility (0.995)
  3. Loci were filtered by call rate (0.95)
  4. Individuals were filtered by call rate (0.80)
  5. SNPs were filtered by read depth (≤ 5 and ≥ 50)
  6. Minor allele frequencies (MAFs) were removed
  7. Monomorphic loci were filtered out
  8. Missing data was imputed using nearest neighbour function
For step 8 I got the message in R that two individuals were filled randomly drawing for the global allele profiles by locus as there were no more individuals left to impute. When trying to look up online if this is common practice I couldn't find much information on this. Is there any clarification on why the "random" method is used for 2 of my samples and is it possible to chance this?

Thank you!
Kind regards,
Chiara

messages.author: d87216285ace7535
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] neighbour impute uses random method for some samples
parts:
G'day Chiara

Assuming you filtered in the order you provided below, I would be do it
in a different order to increase the number of loci retained.

I would first work out which individuals have too much missing data and
exclude them as the first step. Having them in your filtering will
reduce the number of loci retained as they drive all values down as they
contain the most missing data.

I would then do filter by read depth (≤ 5 and ≥ 50), followed by Minor
allele frequencies (MAFs).

Next step is to filter out monomorphic loci.

Then filter on reproducability, then filter by called rate by loci.

That order should give you the highest number of loci.

It often pays to try filtering in slightly different orders as sometimes
it will help increase the number of loci. Eliminating individuals with
too much missing data before you start other filtering is best though in
my mind.

Cheers
Peter Unmack

Chiara

parts:
G'day Chiara

Your step 4. Individuals were filtered by call rate (0.80) is removing
any individuals from the dataset with 20% or more missing data. These
should be removed first as not doing so will likely reduce the number of
loci you end up with. Could only be very minor if it's just a couple
individuals, but why throw any loci away if you can avoid it.

I'm sorry, I've never messed with imputing so I can't be of any help on
that front.

cheers
Peter Unmack
